fatal_errors: The proposed Hf-to-Al substitution does not reconstruct the targeted addition of 4.2 at.% Cr and the resulting approximately 4 vol.% reticulated Laves phase.

The composition (Hf0.9Al0.1)MoTaTiZr contains only about 2 at.% Al overall, so it is inconsistent with an intervention described as 10 at.% substitution unless explicitly defined as replacing 10% of the Hf sublattice.
The claim that Al will preserve BCC phase stability and high-temperature strength is unsupported by the preceding RHEA evidence or any cited evidence.
Allowing either tensile or compressive testing makes the mechanical comparison non-equivalent to the room-temperature compression target.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad density–performance trade-off and proposes a controlled baseline comparison with numerical rejection thresholds, but it is not an evidence-supported reconstruction. The target intervention is Cr addition by vacuum arc melting, producing a small fraction of interconnected Cr2(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) Laves phase plus lattice contraction and solid-solution hardening. The generated proposal instead substitutes Al, assumes without support that the original microstructure and 1000 °C performance will be retained, and predicts merely bounded degradation rather than the observed concurrent gains in yield strength and fracture strain. It also omits the decisive morphology, phase-fraction, lattice-parameter, hardness, and dislocation measurements needed to test the target mechanism. Its experiment can reject a general performance-retention claim, but cannot discriminate solid-solution effects from phase-mediated crack hindrance.
